**Reading map:** Deisenroth, Faisal & Ong, *Mathematics for Machine Learning* (2020), §2.8. This is an original lesson using our delivery-operations example—not reproduced textbook content.

## Why the concept matters

The intercept 3 minutes in a delivery-time predictor represents a fixed handling cost. This constant shifts a linear relation without changing its direction; the result is an affine map.

## Define the mathematical relationship

$$
f(\boldsymbol x)=A\boldsymbol x+\boldsymbol b,\qquad \mathcal A=\boldsymbol x_0+V
$$

The displayed relationship is the main object to analyse. Specify the relevant dimensions, quantities and assumptions before using it. It should be read as a mathematical statement, not merely a programming shorthand.

## Work through an original example

Compare g(d,n)=2d+2n with f(d,n)=3+2d+2n. At (0,0), g=0 but f=3. The set of points satisfying d+n=3 is an affine line, not a subspace, because it excludes the origin.

## What follows, and what does not

Homogeneous coordinates encode affine maps using an extra constant feature: (1,d,n). This explains why the design matrix has a leading column of ones.

## Test your reasoning

Write the affine function f(d,n)=3+2d+2n as one dot product.
